source: Seoul National University Korean 2B, Unit 16, tracks 62-71

lines.ko: 주말인데 표가 있을까요?
걱정하지 마세요. 제가 예매해 놓았어요.
설날에 먹는 특별한 음식이 있어요?
네, 설날에는 밥 대신 떡국을 먹어요.
지연 씨, 이번 연휴에 고향에 내려가요?
네, 한 달 전에 미리 기차표를 예매해 놓았어요.
그렇게 빨리 예매를 해야 돼요?
네, 명절에는 고향에 가는 사람들이 많아서 서두르지 않으면 표 사기가 힘들어요.
그런데 한국에서는 설날에 보통 뭘 해요?
아침에 음식을 차려 놓고 차례를 지내요. 그리고 어른들께 세배를 해요.
설날에 먹는 특별한 음식이 있어요?
설날에는 밥 대신 떡국을 먹어요.
지연 씨도 떡국 끓일 줄 알아요?
그럼요. 나중에 우리 집에 오면 제가 해 줄게요.
이번 연휴에 뭐 할 거예요?
글쎄요. 가까운 곳으로 여행 갈까 해요.
제가 청소를 할까요?
청소는 제가 할 테니까 설거지 좀 해 주세요.

tracks.secEn: Inviting the class over for Chuseok

lines.ko: 이번 추석 연휴에 뭐 할 거야?
글쎄, 아직 잘 모르겠는데.
그럼, 토요일에 반 친구들을 초대할까 하는데 너도 올래?
재미있겠다. 나도 갈게. 내가 뭐 도와줄 거 있어?
그럼 음식 준비하는 것 좀 도와줄래?
그래. 뭘 만들 건데?
송편을 만들까 하는데 해 본 적이 없어서 잘할 수 있을지 모르겠어.
나 송편 만들 줄 알아. 내가 도와줄 테니까 걱정하지 마.
잘됐다. 그럼 내가 장을 미리 봐 놓을게.
그래, 그럼 토요일에 보자.

tracks.secEn: Live from Seoul Station on the eve of Chuseok

lines.ko: 오늘부터 추석 연휴가 시작되는데요. 서울역에 나가 있는 김혜경 기자를 불러 보겠습니다. 김혜경 기자!
예, 저는 지금 서울역에 나와 있습니다. 서울역은 지금 고향에 내려가는 사람들로 복잡합니다. 그럼 고향에 가시는 한 분과 이야기 나눠 보겠습니다. 고향이 어디십니까?
부산입니다.
고향에는 누가 계십니까?
부모님과 형님이 계십니다.
고향에 내려가는 기분이 어떠십니까?
오랫동안 고향에 못 내려갔는데 가족들을 만날 생각을 하니까 아주 기쁩니다. 부모님께서 맛있는 음식도 많이 해 놓고 기다리고 계실 겁니다.
연휴가 긴데, 특별한 계획 있으십니까?
부모님 일도 좀 도와 드리고 가까운 곳으로 여행도 갈까 합니다.
네, 말씀 감사합니다. 고향 잘 다녀오시기 바랍니다. 지금까지 서울역에서 김혜경이었습니다.

tracks.secEn: Finding someone to mind the cat

lines.ko: 정우 씨, 저 나나인데요. 부탁 하나만 해도 돼요?
무슨 일인데요?
제가 추석 연휴에 이틀 정도 여행을 가는데 고양이를 맡길 곳이 없어서요. 미안하지만 고양이 좀 맡아 줄 수 있어요?
아, 어떻게 하죠? 저도 그러고 싶은데 우리 가족도 고향에 내려가요.
그래요? 부탁할 사람이 없어서 큰일이네요.
지연 씨한테 연락해 보면 어때요? 지연 씨 집에도 고양이가 있어요.
아, 그래요? 그럼 한번 전화해 볼게요.
여보세요? 지연 씨? 저 나나인데요. 혹시 이번 연휴에 고향에 내려가요?
아니요, 이번에는 연휴가 짧아서 안 내려가요.
그럼 미안하지만 제 고양이 이틀만 맡아 줄 수 있어요? 여행을 가는데 고양이를 맡길 곳이 없어서요.
네, 좋아요. 제가 잘 봐 줄 테니까 걱정 마세요.
정말 고마워요. 필요한 건 제가 다 준비해서 내일 갈게요.
설날 아침에는 세배를 해요.
일 년 전에 한국에 왔어요.
일 년 후에 다시 만나요.
사물놀이 공연을 본 적이 있어요.
사진이 잘 나왔네요.
이번 설날에 고향에 가요?
네, 고향 갈 날만 기다리고 있어요.

keep: a whole sentence someone would actually say
5-22 syllables: long enough to need listening, short enough to hold in your head

carries at least one thing you can only write correctly if you know something — the unit's grammar (V-아/어 놓다, N 대신, V-(으)ㄹ까 하다, A/V-(으)ㄹ 테니까), a gap between sound and spelling (this unit's 발음 point is 유음화: an initial ㄴ next to a ㄹ is read [ㄹ], so 설날 is [설랄], 일 년 is [일련], 연락 is [열락] and 서울역 is [서울력] — and the rule runs both ways round the ㄹ), or a unit headword
drop: fixed courtesies — 네, 말씀 감사합니다, 여보세요
bare reactions — 무슨 일인데요?, 아, 어떻게 하죠?
proper nouns standing alone: 부산입니다 is five syllables of place name with nothing to decide
anything under ~5 syllables: nothing to decide when you write it
filter.splitAtClause: Printed turns past 22 syllables are cut at a boundary the recording itself pauses on — never mid-clause and never trimmed — and each part names its parent in splitFrom. One sentence of track 68 is dropped rather than cut: 부모님께서 맛있는 음식도 많이 해 놓고 기다리고 계실 겁니다 is 25 syllables read in a single unbroken span, so there is nowhere the recording agrees to cut it.

items.en: It’s the weekend — do you think there are any tickets?
items.why: 있을까요 is said [이쓸까요]. The ㄹ of the ending tenses the ㄱ behind it, so the 까 you hear is already a 까 — but the ㅆ of 있다 has crossed into the next syllable and is not where it sounds.

items.en: Don’t worry. I booked it in advance.
items.why: The page’s own V-아/어 놓다 — the booking is done and the ticket is still there. 걱정 is said [걱쩡], the ㄱ tensing the ㅈ behind it, and 놓았어요 is said [노아써요] with the ㅎ gone between vowels.

items.en: Is there any special food eaten on Seollal?
items.why: The chapter’s 발음 point in its commonest word: 설날 is said [설랄], the ㄴ turning into [ㄹ] after the 받침 ㄹ. 먹는 is said [멍는] on top of it, so two of the four words are spelt nothing like they sound.

items.ko: 네, 설날에는 밥 대신 떡국을 먹어요.
items.en: On Seollal we eat rice-cake soup instead of rice.
items.why: The chapter title, and its own N 대신. 설날 is [설랄] again and 떡국 is [떡꾹] — the ㄱ tenses after the 받침 ㄱ — so the second half is written with plain letters and heard with tense ones.

items.ko: 지연 씨, 이번 연휴에 고향에 내려가요?
items.en: Jiyeon, are you going down to your hometown this long weekend?
items.why: 연휴 and 고향 are both chapter headwords, and both lose a consonant to the vowel after it: 연휴에 runs as [여뉴에] and 고향에 as [고향에] with the ㅇ carrying over. What you hear gives no clue where the word boundaries are.

items.ko: 네, 한 달 전에 미리 기차표를 예매해 놓았어요.
items.en: Yes, I booked the train tickets a month ago.
items.why: V-아/어 놓다 again, this time with the state it leaves behind spelled out: the booking was a month ago and the ticket is still booked. 기차표 is a chapter headword and 놓았어요 is heard as [노아써요].

items.en: Do you need to book that early?
items.why: 그렇게 is said [그러케]: the ㅎ of 그렇다 and the ㄱ of 게 fuse into one aspirated [ㅋ]. Neither letter survives in the sound, so both have to come from knowing the word.

items.ko: 네, 명절에는 고향에 가는 사람들이 많아서
items.en: Yes, because so many people go to their hometown for the holidays,
items.why: 많아서 is said [마나서] — the ㅎ of 많다 goes between vowels and the ㄴ of the cluster carries over — so nothing in the sound says there is an ㅎ to write. 명절 is the chapter’s own headword.
items.splitFrom: 네, 명절에는 고향에 가는 사람들이 많아서 서두르지 않으면 표 사기가 힘들어요.

items.en: if we don’t hurry it will be hard to get a ticket.
items.why: 않으면 is said [아느면], the ㅎ lost between vowels for the second time in one turn. 서두르지 is a 르 stem written out in full here, which is the only place it looks like its dictionary form.
items.splitFrom: 네, 명절에는 고향에 가는 사람들이 많아서 서두르지 않으면 표 사기가 힘들어요.

items.ko: 그런데 한국에서는 설날에 보통 뭘 해요?
items.en: By the way, what do Koreans normally do on Seollal?
items.why: 설날 [설랄] once more, and 뭘 is 무엇을 squeezed into one syllable — a contraction that is written the short way and can only be expanded by someone who knows what it came from.

items.ko: 아침에 음식을 차려 놓고 차례를 지내요.
items.en: In the morning we set the table with food and perform the ancestral rites.
items.why: Two chapter headwords in one clause, and V-아/어 놓다 doing its real work: the food is set out and then left set out while the rites are held. 놓고 is heard as [노코], the ㅎ fusing with the ㄱ.
items.splitFrom: 아침에 음식을 차려 놓고 차례를 지내요. 그리고 어른들께 세배를 해요.

items.en: And we do the New Year’s bow to our elders.
items.why: 어른들께 takes 께 and not 에게, because the elders are the ones being honoured — a choice you can only write correctly if you know who is being spoken about. 세배 is the chapter headword.
items.splitFrom: 아침에 음식을 차려 놓고 차례를 지내요. 그리고 어른들께 세배를 해요.

items.ko: 지연 씨도 떡국 끓일 줄 알아요?
items.en: Jiyeon, do you know how to make tteokguk?
items.why: 끓일 is said [끄릴]. The cluster 받침 ㅀ keeps only its ㄹ, which then crosses into the next syllable, so two of the three letters written in 끓 are silent.

items.ko: 그럼요. 나중에 우리 집에 오면 제가 해 줄게요.
items.en: Of course. I’ll make it for you when you come to my place next time.
items.why: 그럼요 is said [그럼뇨] — a ㄴ appears out of nowhere between the 받침 ㅁ and the 요 — and 줄게요 is said [줄께요]. Both are heard with a sound the spelling does not have.

items.en: What are you going to do this long weekend?
items.why: 할 거예요 is said [할 꺼예요]: the ㄹ of the ending tenses the ㄱ of 거. The tense sound is the rule doing its work, and writing 꺼 would be writing the sound instead of the word.

items.ko: 글쎄요. 가까운 곳으로 여행 갈까 해요.
items.en: Well, I am thinking of travelling somewhere close by.
items.why: The page’s own V-(으)ㄹ까 하다 — a plan that is still only a thought. 곳으로 is said [고스로], the 받침 ㅅ crossing over as a plain [ㅅ] where 곳 on its own would end in [ㄷ].

items.en: Shall I do the cleaning?
items.why: 할까요 is said [할까요] with the ㄱ already tense, so the ㄹ has done its work before you write anything. The 까 is the offer, and 하까요 is what it sounds like it could be.

items.ko: 청소는 제가 할 테니까 설거지 좀 해 주세요.
items.en: I will do the cleaning, so could you wash the dishes.
items.why: The page’s own A/V-(으)ㄹ 테니까: I will take one job, so you take the other. 할 테니까 is said [할 떼니까] with the ㅌ tensed after the ㄹ, and 설거지 is a chapter headword heard as [설거지].

items.ko: 이번 추석 연휴에 뭐 할 거야?
items.en: What are you going to do this Chuseok holiday?
items.why: 거야 is the 반말 of 거예요, and the two are a syllable apart in sound and a whole register apart in use. 추석 is said [추석] but tenses nothing after it here, where 추석도 would.

items.en: Well, I don’t know yet.
items.why: 모르겠는데 is said [모르겐는데]: the ㅆ of 겠 becomes [ㄷ] and then a [ㄴ] in front of the ㄴ. The 겠 that carries the whole guess is the part that disappears.

items.ko: 그럼, 토요일에 반 친구들을 초대할까 하는데 너도 올래?
items.en: Then I’m thinking of inviting my classmates over — do you want to come?
items.why: V-(으)ㄹ까 하다 with 하는데 rather than 해요, which is how the plan gets offered instead of just announced. 친구들을 runs as [친구드를] and 올래 as [올래], the ㄹ doubling across the seam.

items.ko: 재미있겠다. 나도 갈게. 내가 뭐 도와줄 거 있어?
items.en: That sounds fun. I’ll go. Is there anything I can help with?
items.why: 재미있겠다 is said [재미읻께따] and 갈게 is said [갈께] — three tensed consonants in a row that are all written plain. Nothing in the sound tells you where the 있 or the 겠 ends.

items.ko: 그럼 음식 준비하는 것 좀 도와줄래?
items.en: Then will you come and help me get the food ready?
items.why: 것 좀 is said [걷쫌]: the 받침 ㅅ closes as [ㄷ] and tenses the ㅈ behind it. Two syllables, two changes, and the 것 is a bound noun that has to be written separately.

items.en: All right. What are you making?
items.why: 만들 건데 is said [만들 껀데], the ㄹ tensing the ㄱ across the space. 뭘 is 무엇을 again, and the space before 건데 is the one thing the sound cannot tell you.

items.ko: 송편을 만들까 하는데 해 본 적이 없어서
items.en: I’m thinking of making songpyeon, but I have never made it,
items.why: V-(으)ㄹ까 하다 with a chapter headword in front of it. 적이 is said [저기] — the 받침 ㄱ crosses over — so the bound noun 적 and the particle 이 sound like one word that is not either of them.
items.splitFrom: 송편을 만들까 하는데 해 본 적이 없어서 잘할 수 있을지 모르겠어.

items.en: so I’m not sure I can do it well.
items.why: 잘할 수 is said [잘할 쑤] and 있을지 is said [이쓸찌]: the ㄹ tenses whatever follows it twice in five syllables, and both are written with the plain letter.
items.splitFrom: 송편을 만들까 하는데 해 본 적이 없어서 잘할 수 있을지 모르겠어.

items.ko: 나 송편 만들 줄 알아. 내가 도와줄 테니까 걱정하지 마.
items.en: I know how to make songpyeon. I’ll help you, so don’t worry.
items.why: Both of the chapter’s promise forms in one turn: 만들 줄 알아 for the skill and 도와줄 테니까 for the offer. 줄 테니까 is said [줄 떼니까], tensed after the ㄹ like everything else in this unit.

items.ko: 잘됐다. 그럼 내가 장을 미리 봐 놓을게.
items.en: That’s great. Then I’ll do the shopping in advance.
items.why: 장을 미리 봐 놓다 is the chapter’s own phrase and its own grammar at once — the shopping gets done early and stays done. 잘됐다 is said [잘뒏따] with the ㅆ closing as [ㄷ] and tensing the ㄷ behind it.

items.en: All right, see you on Saturday then.
items.why: 보자 is the 반말 suggestion, one syllable away from 보자고 and from 봐요, and none of the three sounds like the others. 토요일에 runs as [토요이레].

items.en: The Chuseok holiday starts today.
items.why: 연휴가 runs as [여뉴가] — the 받침 ㄴ crosses into the 휴 and the word boundary vanishes. 시작되는데요 is the news register’s -는데요, which softens a statement into an opening.
items.splitFrom: 오늘부터 추석 연휴가 시작되는데요. 서울역에 나가 있는 김혜경 기자를 불러 보겠습니다. 김혜경 기자!

items.ko: 예, 저는 지금 서울역에 나와 있습니다.
items.en: Yes, I am at Seoul Station now.
items.why: 서울역 is said [서울력]: the chapter’s 유음화 turning the ㅇ-initial 역 into [력] after the 받침 ㄹ. With 에 behind it the whole thing runs as [서울려게], and not one syllable is where it sounds.
items.splitFrom: 예, 저는 지금 서울역에 나와 있습니다. 서울역은 지금 고향에 내려가는 사람들로 복잡합니다. 그럼 고향에 가시는 한 분과 이야기 나눠 보겠습니다. 고향이 어디십니까?

items.ko: 서울역은 지금 고향에 내려가는 사람들로 복잡합니다.
items.en: Seoul Station is busy right now with people heading down to their hometowns.
items.why: 서울역 is [서울력] first, so 서울역은 comes out [서울려근], and 복잡합니다 is [복짜팜니다] — the ㄱ tenses the ㅈ, the ㅂ fuses with the ㅎ, and the ㅂ of 합 becomes [ㅁ] before the ㄴ. Four letters change and none of them may be written as heard.
items.splitFrom: 예, 저는 지금 서울역에 나와 있습니다. 서울역은 지금 고향에 내려가는 사람들로 복잡합니다. 그럼 고향에 가시는 한 분과 이야기 나눠 보겠습니다. 고향이 어디십니까?

items.ko: 그럼 고향에 가시는 한 분과 이야기 나눠 보겠습니다.
items.en: Let me talk to one of the people going home.
items.why: 가시는 carries the 시 that honours the traveller and 보겠습니다 the 겠 that offers the action — two grammatical syllables that change nothing audible about the verbs they sit on.
items.splitFrom: 예, 저는 지금 서울역에 나와 있습니다. 서울역은 지금 고향에 내려가는 사람들로 복잡합니다. 그럼 고향에 가시는 한 분과 이야기 나눠 보겠습니다. 고향이 어디십니까?

items.en: Where is your hometown?
items.why: 어디십니까 is 어디 plus the honorific 시 plus the 합쇼체 question ending, and it is said [어디심니까] with the ㅂ turning into [ㅁ]. The ㅂ that is written is the one you never hear.
items.splitFrom: 예, 저는 지금 서울역에 나와 있습니다. 서울역은 지금 고향에 내려가는 사람들로 복잡합니다. 그럼 고향에 가시는 한 분과 이야기 나눠 보겠습니다. 고향이 어디십니까?

items.en: Who is there in your hometown?
items.why: 계십니까 is said [계심니까]: the 받침 ㅂ becomes [ㅁ] in front of the ㄴ, the same change as in 합니다. 계시다 is the honorific of 있다 and shares none of its letters.

items.en: My parents and my older brother are there.
items.why: 형님이 runs as [형니미] and 계십니다 is [계심니다]. 님 is the honorific suffix on both nouns, and it is the part a learner writing by ear leaves off.

items.en: How does it feel to be going home?
items.why: 내려가다 is the chapter’s own word for going home — down from the capital, whatever the map says. 어떠십니까 is 어떻다 with the ㅎ gone before the 시, so the adjective it comes from is not visible in it.

items.en: I have not been able to go home for a long time,
items.why: 못 내려갔는데 is said [몬 내려간는데]: the 받침 ㅅ of 못 becomes [ㄴ] before the ㄴ, and the ㅆ of 갔 does the same. 오랫동안 is [오랟똥안] with a tensed ㄷ. Nothing is spelt as it sounds.
items.splitFrom: 오랫동안 고향에 못 내려갔는데 가족들을 만날 생각을 하니까 아주 기쁩니다. 부모님께서 맛있는 음식도 많이 해 놓고 기다리고 계실 겁니다.

items.ko: 가족들을 만날 생각을 하니까 아주 기쁩니다.
items.en: so I am very glad at the thought of seeing my family.
items.why: 생각을 runs as [생가글] and 기쁩니다 is said [기쁨니다]. 만날 is the future-modifier form of 만나다, one letter away from the plain 만나 and carrying the whole "about to" of the sentence.
items.splitFrom: 오랫동안 고향에 못 내려갔는데 가족들을 만날 생각을 하니까 아주 기쁩니다. 부모님께서 맛있는 음식도 많이 해 놓고 기다리고 계실 겁니다.

items.en: The holiday is long — do you have any special plans?
items.why: 있으십니까 is said [이쓰심니까]: the ㅆ crosses over, the honorific 시 sits inside, and the ㅂ becomes [ㅁ]. 특별한 is [특뼈란], the ㅂ tensed after the ㄱ and the ㅎ gone.

items.en: I am going to help my parents with their work a bit,
items.why: 도와 드리다 is the humble half of 도와주다 — the same help, offered upwards — and the 드 is the only thing on the page that says so. 일도 runs as [일또] with the ㄷ tensed after the ㄹ.
items.splitFrom: 부모님 일도 좀 도와 드리고 가까운 곳으로 여행도 갈까 합니다.

items.en: and travel somewhere close by as well.
items.why: The chapter’s V-(으)ㄹ까 하다 in its 합쇼체 form, which is the register the whole interview is in. 곳으로 is said [고스로], the 받침 ㅅ crossing as a plain [ㅅ] where 곳 alone would end in [ㄷ].
items.splitFrom: 부모님 일도 좀 도와 드리고 가까운 곳으로 여행도 갈까 합니다.

items.en: I hope you have a good trip home.
items.why: 다녀오시기 바랍니다 is a wish, not an instruction: the 기 turns the verb into a noun and 바라다 does the hoping. 바랍니다 is said [바람니다], the ㅂ becoming [ㅁ] again.
items.splitFrom: 네, 말씀 감사합니다. 고향 잘 다녀오시기 바랍니다. 지금까지 서울역에서 김혜경이었습니다.

items.en: That was Kim Hyegyeong, reporting from Seoul Station.
items.why: 서울역에서 is said [서울려게서]: 유음화 makes 서울역 into [서울력] first, and then the ㄱ crosses into the 에, so the one word runs five syllables with no seam you can hear.
items.splitFrom: 네, 말씀 감사합니다. 고향 잘 다녀오시기 바랍니다. 지금까지 서울역에서 김혜경이었습니다.

items.ko: 정우 씨, 저 나나인데요. 부탁 하나만 해도 돼요?
items.en: Jeongu, it’s Nana. May I ask you a favour?
items.why: 해도 돼요 is permission asked, and 돼요 is 되어요 contracted — one syllable that two have been folded into. 부탁 is the chapter headword the whole conversation turns on.

items.ko: 제가 추석 연휴에 이틀 정도 여행을 가는데
items.en: I am going away for about two days over Chuseok,
items.why: 여행을 runs as [여행을] with the ㅇ carrying nothing, but 연휴에 runs as [여뉴에] and 이틀 as [이틀]. 정도 is "about", and writing 정도 rather than 쯤 is a choice the sound does not make for you.
items.splitFrom: 제가 추석 연휴에 이틀 정도 여행을 가는데 고양이를 맡길 곳이 없어서요. 미안하지만 고양이 좀 맡아 줄 수 있어요?

items.ko: 미안하지만 고양이 좀 맡아 줄 수 있어요?
items.en: I am sorry to ask, but could you look after my cat?
items.why: 맡아 is said [마타]: the 받침 ㅌ crosses into the vowel and stays aspirated, so the ㅌ is heard in the wrong syllable. 맡다 and 막다 and 맞다 all end up [마−] somewhere, and only the spelling separates them.
items.splitFrom: 제가 추석 연휴에 이틀 정도 여행을 가는데 고양이를 맡길 곳이 없어서요. 미안하지만 고양이 좀 맡아 줄 수 있어요?

items.ko: 저도 그러고 싶은데 우리 가족도 고향에 내려가요.
items.en: I would like to, but my family is going home too.
items.why: 싶은데 runs as [시픈데], the 받침 ㅍ crossing over, and 가족도 is [가족또] with the ㄷ tensed after the ㄱ. The refusal is done entirely with 도 — me too, us too — and never with a no.
items.splitFrom: 아, 어떻게 하죠? 저도 그러고 싶은데 우리 가족도 고향에 내려가요.

items.en: Really? It’s a real problem — there is no one left to ask.
items.why: 큰일이네요 is said [큰니리네요]. A ㄴ appears between 큰 and 일 that neither word contains, and then the ㄹ of 일 crosses into the 이. The chapter headword is the hardest word here to write from the sound.

items.en: Why not try getting in touch with Jiyeon?
items.why: 연락 is said [열락]: the chapter’s 유음화 running the other way round, with the 받침 ㄴ turning into [ㄹ] before the ㄹ that follows. Write what you hear and the word becomes 열락, which is not a word.
items.splitFrom: 지연 씨한테 연락해 보면 어때요? 지연 씨 집에도 고양이가 있어요.

items.en: Jiyeon has a cat at her place too.
items.why: 집에도 runs as [지베도] — the 받침 ㅂ crosses into the 에 — so the 집 that carries the meaning is the syllable you cannot hear the end of.
items.splitFrom: 지연 씨한테 연락해 보면 어때요? 지연 씨 집에도 고양이가 있어요.

items.ko: 아, 그래요? 그럼 한번 전화해 볼게요.
items.en: Oh, really? Then I’ll try phoning her.
items.why: 볼게요 is said [볼께요] and 한번 is said [한번] as one word, where 한 번 with a space would be "one time". The space is the whole difference and there is none of it in the sound.

items.en: Are you by any chance going home this holiday?
items.why: 혹시 is said [혹씨], the ㅅ tensed after the 받침 ㄱ, and it is the word that turns a question into a careful one. 연휴에 runs as [여뉴에] again.
items.splitFrom: 여보세요? 지연 씨? 저 나나인데요. 혹시 이번 연휴에 고향에 내려가요?

items.ko: 아니요, 이번에는 연휴가 짧아서 안 내려가요.
items.en: No, the holiday is short this time, so I am not going.
items.why: 짧아서 is said [짤바서]. The cluster 받침 ㄼ sounds only its ㄹ on its own, but a vowel behind it wakes the ㅂ and sends it into the next syllable — so both letters are heard, in the wrong places.

items.ko: 그럼 미안하지만 제 고양이 이틀만 맡아 줄 수 있어요?
items.en: Then I am sorry to ask, but could you mind my cat for two days?
items.why: 이틀만 is [이틀만] and 맡아 is [마타] once more. 줄 수 있어요 is the whole ability construction spelt out, and it is said [줄 쑤 이써요] with two tensings and a crossing.
items.splitFrom: 그럼 미안하지만 제 고양이 이틀만 맡아 줄 수 있어요? 여행을 가는데 고양이를 맡길 곳이 없어서요.

items.ko: 여행을 가는데 고양이를 맡길 곳이 없어서요.
items.en: I am going away and have nowhere to leave my cat.
items.why: 맡길 is said [맏낄]: the 받침 ㅌ closes as [ㄷ] and tenses the ㄱ behind it, so neither of the two letters written is the one you hear. 곳이 runs as [고시].
items.splitFrom: 그럼 미안하지만 제 고양이 이틀만 맡아 줄 수 있어요? 여행을 가는데 고양이를 맡길 곳이 없어서요.

items.ko: 네, 좋아요. 제가 잘 봐 줄 테니까 걱정 마세요.
items.en: Yes, of course. I’ll take good care of it, so don’t worry.
items.why: The chapter’s A/V-(으)ㄹ 테니까 used to reassure rather than to divide work. 좋아요 is said [조아요] with the ㅎ gone between vowels, and 줄 테니까 is [줄 떼니까].

items.ko: 정말 고마워요. 필요한 건 제가 다 준비해서 내일 갈게요.
items.en: Thank you so much. I’ll get everything it needs ready and come tomorrow.
items.why: 필요한 is said [피료한], the ㄹ crossing into the 요, and 건 is 것은 contracted to one syllable. 갈게요 is [갈께요] with the ㄱ tensed after the ㄹ.

items.en: On Seollal morning we do the New Year’s bow.
items.why: The 발음 page’s first example. 설날 is said [설랄]: the ㄴ of 날 becomes [ㄹ] after the 받침 ㄹ of 설. Write the sound and you get 설랄, which is not the holiday.

items.en: I came to Korea a year ago.
items.why: 일 년 is said [일련] — the same rule across a space this time, which is why the space survives in writing and not in sound. 한국에 runs as [한구게].

items.en: Let’s meet again a year from now.
items.why: 일 년 [일련] again, and 후에 runs straight on after it, so the three words are heard as one five-syllable run with no boundary anywhere in it.

items.en: I have seen a samulnori performance.
items.why: 사물놀이 is said [사물로리]: 유음화 turns the 놀 into [롤], and then its ㄹ crosses into the 이. Four syllables written, four heard, and not one of them the same.

items.en: The photo came out well.
items.why: 잘 나왔네요 is said [잘라완네요]. The ㄴ of 나 becomes [ㄹ] after the 받침 ㄹ of 잘, and then the ㅆ of 왔 becomes [ㄴ] before the 네 — two different rules inside four syllables.

items.en: Are you going to your hometown this Seollal?
items.why: 설날에 is said [설라레]: 유음화 makes 설날 into [설랄] first, and then the new [ㄹ] crosses into the 에. The 날 that is written has neither of its letters left where they started.

items.ko: 네, 고향 갈 날만 기다리고 있어요.
items.en: Yes, I am just waiting for the day I go home.
items.why: 갈 날만 is said [갈랄만]: 유음화 across the space, and then the 받침 ㄹ of 날 holds while the ㅁ follows. 날 is the chapter headword and the hardest three syllables on the page.

listenOnly: Every track carries a script: the unit pages print them for the grammar, 말하기 and 발음 tracks, and the 듣기 지문 at the back of the book prints the two 듣기 conversations.
